fixes.explanation: You got it, baker, the holy garments are for Aaron. Verse 1 says they make "…as well as the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:1) Nothing about them is left to guess. Aaron gets a whole set of holy garments, and my wardrobe is a hat and an apron.

Moses is a fair guess, but the holy garments aren't for him. Exodus 39:1 says they make "…the holy garments for Aaron…" The same verse says they did it just as the LORD had commanded Moses. So Moses is the one the commands were given to, and Aaron is the one the garments are for.

Joshua is a good name, but this verse doesn't mention him. Exodus 39:1 says they make "…the holy garments for Aaron…" The text names Aaron, and that's who they're for. I'd love to give you Joshua, but I can't argue with the verse.

Not quite, baker, because the workers don't design these garments however they think looks best. Verse 1 says they made the garments "…just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:1) So the plan came from the LORD's command. That makes the statement false.

That's it, baker, they hammer it thin and cut threads. Verse 3 says, "They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them to interweave with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen…" (Exodus 39:3) That means real gold thread goes right into the weave. The text calls it the work of a skilled craftsman, and I believe it.

Grinding gold into dye is a creative idea, but the text doesn't say that. Exodus 39:3 says they "…hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them…" Those threads were interwoven with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen. So the gold goes in as real thread, not as color.

That's true, baker, the waistband is one piece with the ephod. Verse 5 says the waistband "…was of one piece with the ephod, of the same workmanship…" (Exodus 39:5) So it isn't a separate belt added on. It was made just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Right, the stones carry the names of the sons of Israel. Exodus 39:6 says they were "…engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel." The same verse says the onyx stones were mounted in gold filigree settings. That's careful work in onyx and gold.

The Ten Commandments are a big deal, but they aren't what's carved on these stones. Exodus 39:6 says the onyx stones were engraved "…with the names of the sons of Israel." So these stones carry names, not commandments. The commandments just aren't part of this verse.

Moses and Aaron are two names we've heard a lot, but they aren't the ones on these stones. Verse 6 says the onyx stones were engraved "…with the names of the sons of Israel." (Exodus 39:6) Those are the names carved there. So Moses and Aaron aren't the answer this time.

Yes, the word is memorial, baker. Verse 7 says they fastened the stones on the shoulder pieces "…as memorial stones for the sons of Israel…" (Exodus 39:7) That's the word the text gives. They did it as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Foundation is a solid word, but it isn't the one in the verse. Exodus 39:7 says the stones were fastened on the shoulder pieces "…as memorial stones for the sons of Israel…" So the word is memorial. Foundation stones hold up a building, and these sit on the ephod's shoulder pieces.

Boundary stones are a real thing, but this verse uses a different word. Exodus 39:7 says these were "…memorial stones for the sons of Israel…" So the word that fits is memorial. Same stones, and the text picks memorial.

That's true, baker. Verse 8 says, "He made the breastpiece with the same workmanship as the ephod, with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen." (Exodus 39:8) The breastpiece and the ephod share the same materials and the same workmanship. So the two pieces match.

It's actually true, baker. Exodus 39:8 says the breastpiece was made "…with the same workmanship as the ephod…" The verse lists gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. So the two pieces match.

Yes, each stone carries the name of one tribe. Verse 14 says each stone "…was engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) So twelve stones go with twelve tribes. That's a lot of names to get right, and the text says they got it done.

A promise would be lovely, but that isn't what's on the stones. Exodus 39:14 says each stone was engraved "…with the name of one of the twelve tribes." So each stone carries a tribe's name. The verse says nothing about a promise being engraved.

There's no line from the law on these stones. Verse 14 says each of the twelve stones was "…engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) So each stone carries a tribe's name. That's what the verse says is engraved.

That's the reason the text gives, baker. Verse 21 says they tied the rings together with blue cord "…so that the breastpiece was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod…" (Exodus 39:21) So the breastpiece stays above the waistband. They did it just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

The text goes the other direction, friend. Exodus 39:21 says the cord was there so the breastpiece "…would not swing out from the ephod…" That's about keeping it in place. Nothing in the verse says it was meant to come off in a hurry.

Scratching is a fair worry, but the text doesn't give that reason. Verse 21 says they tied the rings with blue cord "…so that the breastpiece was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod…" (Exodus 39:21) That's the reason the verse gives. The cord keeps the breastpiece from swinging out.

Yes, the robe is blue, baker. Verse 22 says, "They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:22) That's one color all the way through the cloth. Other colors show up later, on the hem in verse 24.

Scarlet shows up in these garments, but not as the robe's cloth. Exodus 39:22 says the robe was made "…entirely of blue cloth…" Scarlet yarn does appear in the pomegranates on the lower hem (Exodus 39:24). So the robe itself is blue.

Purple is in the yarn on other pieces, but the robe's cloth is something else. Verse 22 says it was made "…entirely of blue cloth…" (Exodus 39:22) Purple yarn does appear in the pomegranates on the lower hem (Exodus 39:24). So the robe itself is blue.

That's right, baker. Verse 23 says there was "…a collar around the opening so that it would not tear." (Exodus 39:23) So the collar is there to keep the opening from tearing. I've torn a few things by pulling too hard, so I get it.

The text doesn't say anything about height, friend. Exodus 39:23 says the collar was around the opening "…so that it would not tear." That's the reason it gives. The collar is there to keep the opening from tearing.

Nothing in the verse mentions tying. Exodus 39:23 says the collar was around the opening "…so that it would not tear." That's the reason the text gives. So the collar is there to keep the opening from tearing.

That's right, baker, they're bells. Verse 25 says, "They also made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates…" (Exodus 39:25) Verse 26 says the bells and pomegranates alternate around the lower hem. So it goes bell, pomegranate, bell, pomegranate, all the way around.

Cymbals are a fun guess, friend, but the verse names something else. Exodus 39:25 says they made "…bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates…" So the word is bells. Verse 26 says the bells and pomegranates alternate around the lower hem.

Not quite, baker. Verse 27 says, "For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:27) So the tunics are for Aaron and his sons. That makes the statement false, since they aren't for Aaron alone.

Right, it's false, baker. The text says "For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:27) So Aaron's sons get tunics too. The tunics aren't for Aaron alone.

Yes, the words are HOLY TO THE LORD, baker. Verse 30 says they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and they "…engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 39:30) Those are the words the verse gives. The plate is gold, and the message is worth reading twice.

Servant is a good word, but it isn't what's engraved. Exodus 39:30 says the inscription reads "HOLY TO THE LORD." Those are the words on the plate of the holy crown. The verse says that plate is pure gold.

Priest of the LORD sounds like it would fit, but those aren't the words in the text. Verse 30 says they engraved on the plate, "…like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 39:30) So that's the inscription. The plate belongs to the holy crown.

Yes, the turban, baker. Verse 31 says, "Then they fastened to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:31) The blue cord is what mounts the plate. So the gold plate sits on the turban.

The sash is another linen piece, but it isn't where the plate goes. Exodus 39:31 says the blue cord was fastened "…to mount it on the turban…" The sash shows up back in verse 29. So the answer is the turban.

The breastpiece has its own gold and cords, but this plate doesn't mount on it. Verse 31 says the blue cord was fastened to the plate "…to mount it on the turban…" (Exodus 39:31) So the plate goes on the turban. The breastpiece isn't mentioned in this verse.

That's true, baker. Verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:32) That verse comes right after the holy crown. So the text says all the work for the tabernacle is complete.

It's actually true, baker. Right after the holy crown, verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed." (Exodus 39:32) The same verse says the Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. So the work is complete.

That's it, baker. Verse 43 says Moses "…inspected all the work and saw that they had accomplished it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them." (Exodus 39:43) He looks over everything first, and then the blessing comes. The tabernacle story isn't over yet, though.

A day off sounds nice, friend, but the text doesn't say that. Exodus 39:43 says Moses inspected the work and saw they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. Then it says, "So Moses blessed them." That's what he does.

A feast would be fun, and I'd bring cookies, but the verse doesn't say that. Exodus 39:43 says Moses saw they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. Then it says, "So Moses blessed them." A blessing is what the text gives.
